High Court Of Punjab And Haryana
 At Chandigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ramendra Jain
Present:- Mr. Aditya Sanghi, Advocate, for the petitioner.
 Mr. Raj Kumar Makkar, Sr. Dag, Haryana.
Ramendra Jain, J. (Oral)
Custody certificate filed in Court today is taken on record.

Through instant revision, petitioner accused has laid challenge to judgment dated 04.12.2013 of the Appellate Court, affirming the judgment of conviction dated 16.08.2011 and order of sentence dated 18.08.2011 of the Trial Court,
holding him guilty and sentencing to undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months and pay fine of `1,000/- under Section 7 punishable under Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954 (in short the 'Act'), in default of payment of fine to undergo rigorous imprisonment for one month.

Briefly, on 10.05.2001 Government Food Inspector purchased 750 grams of 'dal moong dhuli' out of total quantity of 15 kg kept by the petitioner for sale, on payment of requisite price and converted into three separate parcels, out of which one was sent to Public Analyst, Haryana, Chandigarh, who vide his report dated 11.05.2001 declared the sample mis- branded on account of its coating with tartrazine (a synthetic food colour).

sentences.text:
Consequently, Government 1 of 4 Food Inspector filed a complaint CRR-3908 of 2013 (O&M)
against the petitioner, who after holding trial was convicted and sentenced in the manner as narrated above in the opening part of the judgment.
Being aggrieved, petitioner preferred appeal, but remained unsuccessful, as the same too was dismissed by the Appellate Court vide judgment dated 04.12.2013.

Learned counsel for the petitioner drawing attention of this Court towards Rule 28 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (in short the 'Rules') inter alia contends that both the Courts below have failed to appreciate that addition of tatrazine in 'dal moong dhuli' does not tentamount to food adulteration.
Therefore, without compliance of Section 16-A of the Act, petitioner could not have been convicted.
In support of his contention, learned counsel placed reliance on the judgment of this Court in Hari Ram v. State of Haryana, (2009) 5 RCR (Criminal) 561.

entities.text: Hari Ram v. State of Haryana, (2009) 5 RCR (Criminal) 561
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the other hand, learned State counsel refuting above submissions and pleading legality and validity of the impugned judgments of both the Courts below, referring to Rule 48-A of the Rules urged that petitioner could not have kept 'dal moong dhuli' coloured with tatrazine without any permit or licence, which the petitioner could not produce at any stage.
Having given thoughtful consideration to the rival submissions, this Court finds the instant revision completely devoid of any merit for the reasons to follow.
Petitioner cannot be given benefit of Rule 28 for violating Rule 48 of the Rules, by keeping coloured 'dal moong dhuli' without any permit or licence.

While exercising its revisional powers, this Court has very limited 2 of 4 CRR-3908 of 2013 (O&M)
jurisdiction, which can only be exercised, (i) when the Courts below have acted beyond jurisdiction vested in them or (ii) have not exercised the same diligently and (iii) have exercised illegally.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has not been able to show any such infirmities in the judgments of both the Courts below.

Petitioner was tried, treating complaint of the Government Food Inspector as a warrant case in which there is always more scope for an accused to rebut the evidence of the prosecution by leading evidence in defence unlike summary case, inasmuch as in a warrant case after recording statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. an accused is afforded opportunity to lead his evidence in defence, if any.
Therefore, petitioner on technical ground of non-compliance of Section 16-A of the Act cannot be acquitted by setting aside two judgments of both the Courts below based on appreciation of evidence.

Facts and circumstances of the authority referred to above by learned counsel for the petitioner are not identical to the facts of the present case, inasmuch as petitioner was never given any notice for being tried in a summary case.
He was straightaway, after his summoning, was charge- sheeted to which, he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

Further, as discussed above, he was afforded Mahesh Chander @ Mahesh Chand vs State Of Haryana on 18 March, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14773498/
2 opportunity for leading evidence in his defence.

sentences.text: At this stage, learned counsel referring to the judgment of this Court in Manbir Singh v. State of Haryana (CRR-1237 of 2012) decided on 01.12.2018, prays for reducing the sentence of the petitioner on the ground that this criminal trial is hanging on his head like damocle's sword for more than fifteen years, which is a sufficient mitigating circumstance to treat him 3 of 4 CRR-3908 of 2013 (O&M) leniently.

entities.text: Manbir Singh v. State of Haryana (CRR-1237 of 2012)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner has suffered the ordeal for a long period and has already undergone sentence for one month and eight days.

As far as prayer of learned counsel for the petitioner qua quantum of sentence is concerned, this Court, taking into account the fact that petitioner is facing protracted trial since last around 15 years and is the first offender, his sentence is reduced from six months to three months with increase in fine from `1,000/- to `10,000/-.
On completion of three months and payment of fine, petitioner be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
With above modification, present revision is disposed of.

A copy of this order be sent to the CJM,
Rewari for information and necessary compliance.
(RAMENDRA JAIN)

March 18, 2019 JUDGE R.S.
